thread:
alex.j: Quick q — custody schedule changed midyear, we split weekdays. Can I add my child to Redwood benefits now? Also how do we decide primary vs secondary insurer and what proof do you need?

maria.peopleops: Hi Alex — yes, that typically qualifies as a Qualifying Life Event (QLE). You have 30 days from the event to submit the QLE request and supporting docs.

alex.j: Cool. If my birthday is in Jan and my ex's is in Aug, does that mean I'm primary? And does that apply to medical/dental/vision equally?

maria.peopleops: The common coordination-of-benefits (COB) rule used by carriers is the "birthday rule" — the parent with the earlier birthday in the year is primary. It usually applies to core medical and most ancillaries, but some dental/vision carriers have their own rules. We can confirm for the specific carrier if you want.

alex.j: What docs are accepted? Court order, parenting plan, a handwritten note?

maria.peopleops: Acceptable proofs (most frequent):
- Court order or parenting plan indicating custody change
- Notarized agreement signed by both parents
- School records or government ID showing the child at your address (if residency supports the change)
- Court filing receipt if final order is pending — we can do provisional enrollment while carrier verifies

alex.j: How do I submit? Email? Portal? Any subject line requirements?

maria.peopleops: Please email benefits@redwood.com with subject exactly: "QLE: Add dependent — custody change — <your name>" and attach PDFs. Or upload via People Ops portal > Benefits > QLE uploads. Our benefits-bot will acknowledge.

benefits-bot: Received: If you uploaded, we assigned case #RB-2143. Carrier verification typically takes 5-10 business days.

alex.j: Payroll/proration — if added mid-month, will my deduction be pro-rated or full month?

maria.peopleops: Carriers differ. Typical scenarios:
- If carrier processes before their monthly cutoff, effective date can be backdated to the QLE date and premiums prorated from that date.
- If missed, effective date might be 1st of next month (no retro proration).
We will estimate payroll impact and confirm the deduction amount before it posts.

alex.j: What if my ex's plan already paid for an upcoming appt next week? Any coordination required?

tom.broker: If your plan becomes primary, submit the claim to your primary plan first. If the ex's plan already paid, your plan (as secondary) can request coordination/adjustment. For urgent needs, I can request a predetermination/coverage letter from the carrier; DM me provider/name/date and I'll start it.

alex.j: Thanks — I'll scan the parenting plan and send to benefits@redwood.com now. Can someone ping here once carrier confirms? :thumbsup:

maria.peopleops: Please ping me after you send it and I'll confirm receipt and expected effective date. We can also flag payroll for expedited handling if needed. :wave:
